title: The pullback of module objects preserves K-flat complexes
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of schemes, with pulled-back coefficient rings $\Lambda_Y$ and $f^*\Lambda_Y$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The functor $\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*)\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{f^*\Lambda_Y}$, the transport of module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] along the sheaf pullback $f^*$ [def-sfb-module-upper-star], applied termwise, sends K-flat complexes of $\Lambda_Y$-modules to K-flat complexes of $f^*\Lambda_Y$-modules, K-flatness [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] taken for the relative tensor product of module objects [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor].

source.place: lem-sfb-module-upper-star-kflat-quasi-iso: the Lean of lem-sfb-module-upper-star-kflat-quasi-iso (preservesKFlatQuasiIso_upperStar = Functor.preservesKFlatQuasiIso_comp of mapMod(f^*) and the extension of scalars) uses the instance preservesKFlatComplexes_mapMod_upperStar; module docstring: f^* is strong monoidal, exact and commutes with colimits, so it commutes with the relative tensor product of complexes and preserves acyclicity; Lean: upstream file lean/WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/ProEtale/ModuleObject/Derived/UpperLowerStar.lean, declaration AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.CondensedRing.preservesKFlatComplexes_mapMod_upperStar (module WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.ModuleObject.Derived.UpperLowerStar, lines 174-177, proof `sorry`)

proof.text: Let $P$ be any K-flat complex of $\Lambda_Y$-module objects. Apply [lem-sfb-module-mapmod-pullback-kflat] to the same commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$, schemes $X,Y$ and morphism $f$. Its transport $\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$ is exactly the transport in this statement, with the same source ring $\Lambda_Y$ and target ring $f^*\Lambda_Y$. Its conclusion is K-flatness of the termwise image of $P$ for the relative tensor product of module objects, which is the required conclusion. In particular, it tests all acyclic target-module complexes; no assumption that such a test complex is itself pulled back is made. No extension of scalars along $f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$ is involved.
